notes:
Summary: Axion Zenith is a mid-market product company building an embedded AI assistant across web and mobile. Started on Redwood Hosted API (sep 2024 POC) — moved to Dedicated evaluation for predictable latency and cost at scale. Very concerned about EU data residency and audit controls.

POC + Demo Highlights:
- 3-week hosted POC (sep/oct 2024): validated answer quality and embeddings for search; usage pattern ~= 35 QPS peak, average 12 QPS.
- Hosted p95 latency for 512-token chat ~160ms; target for production is p95 <= 100ms for chat at 50 QPS.
- Dedicated demo week (dec 2024) with Redwood SE: p95 improved to ~95ms using A10-like hosts + continuous batching config.
- KV/prefix cache gave ~18% cost savings on repeated flows.

Requirements (from product + infra leads):
- Workloads: real-time chat (primary), embeddings for search (secondary), occasional reranking for personalization.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 100ms for chat; p99 < 300ms for critical flows.
- Throughput: steady 20–30 QPS, spikes to 120 QPS during campaigns (need burst).
- Cost sensitivity: must hold unit cost predictability; forecast model shows max $300–350k ARR for infra spend.
- Model preferences: open 30B-class models (Redwood-verified), fall back to 7B quantized variants for cost-saving bursts.
- Routing: region-aware routing + fallback to smaller model variant on capacity constraints.

Pricing / Packaging Negotiation Notes:
- Redwood AE proposed 12-month Dedicated commit structure: baseline reserved capacity to cover 60% of forecasted peak; ramp schedule to reach 100% reserved by month 9.
- Proposed commit tiers discussed: Bronze (baseline 60%), Silver (80%), Gold (100%) with graduated discounts on unit token-equivalent and lower burst overage for higher tiers.
- Burst policy draft: allow up to 2.5x baseline for short windows (up to 6 hours/day) with overage billed at 1.6x baseline unit rate, 24h aggregated. Customer pushing for 2x burst at 1.2x rate.
- Overage protections: cap monthly overage at 30% of committed capacity unless pre-approved. Axion asks for emergency unlimited burst fallback to Hosted API at pre-negotiated rate (for extreme events).
- Ramp schedule: client requires predictable monthly ramp (10% month-over-month increase for first 6 months) with option to accelerate into quarter 3 if metrics hold.
- Billing model: Redwood proposed committed GPU-hours equivalent + token-adjustment; Axion pushing for token-based effective rate to match dev forecast models.

Security & Compliance:
- Must have SOC2 Type II or equivalent; Redwood to share SOC2 report and architecture diagram (action item).
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in eu-central region; Redwood to confirm routing and audit logs.
- KMS support mandatory, with customer-managed keys preferred.

Commercials / Open questions:
- Final unit price depends on commit tier — current redline pricing provided in drive doc (AXZ_Redwood_pricing_v3.xlsx).
- Finance wants a 12-month commit with quarterly billing; legal pushing for SLA language on latency/availability and credits tied to p95/p99.
- Team asked for an example SOW and a ramp/capacity test plan to sign off (AE to deliver draft SOW by 2025-01-20).

Direct quotes from stakeholders:
- Head of Platform: "We need predictable bills — can't have random spikes blow our margin."
- CTO: "If we can get dedicated baseline + reasonable burst limits, we avoid building infra ourselves."

Notes on tone / CRM behavior: shorthand in threads, client likes clear SKUs and deterministic cost impact per feature. They push back hard on any surcharge wording (want fixed overage caps).
